PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 19 years
Gestational Age at Sampling: 18 weeks
Indication for Testing: Prenatal trisomy screening
Referring Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]
Referring Hospital: [redacted location]

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Test Code: QFPCR-TRI

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniotic fluid cells for the rapid detection of trisomies 13, 18 and 21. DNA was extracted from 2ml of amniotic fluid using QIAamp DNA Mini Kit. Multiplex PCR amplification was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. A minimum of 4 informative markers per chromosome were analyzed. Fragment analysis was performed on an Applied Biosystems 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak area ratios were calculated for all informative markers.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13 (STR markers: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628):
Result: NORMAL DIALLELIC PATTERN
All informative markers show normal 1:1 peak ratios

Chromosome 18 (STR markers: D18S391, D18S390, D18S535, D18S386):
Result: NORMAL DIALLELIC PATTERN
All informative markers show normal 1:1 peak ratios

Chromosome 21 (STR markers: D21S1435, D21S11, D21S1270, D21S1411):
Result: NORMAL DIALLELIC PATTERN
All informative markers show normal 1:1 peak ratios

Sex Chromosome Markers:
AMELOGENIN: XY pattern detected
Sex chromosome aneuploidy screening: No abnormalities detected

QUALITY METRICS
DNA Concentration: 45 ng/μl
Total DNA Yield: 180 ng
Amplification Success: 100%
Maternal Cell Contamination: Not detected

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates a normal chromosomal complement for chromosomes 13, 18 and 21. No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) was detected in this fetal sample.

The fetal sex is male (XY).

LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y only. It will not detect:
- Balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Mosaicism below 20%
- Structural chromosomal abnormalities
- Aneuploidies of other chromosomes
- Single gene disorders
- Microdeletion/microduplication syndromes

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis from cultured amniocytes to follow. This will provide comprehensive cytogenetic evaluation of all chromosomes and can detect structural abnormalities not identified by QF-PCR.

This result has been discussed with the referring clinician.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
Report Date: [redacted date]
